newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ABS-CBN says advertisers coming back.
newsitem.headline: ABS-CBN says advertisers coming back.

text.p: ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp said on Monday some of its advertisers came back late last week even after a group of companies cancelled their orders to protest a 22 percent increase in rates.

"On the evening of March 13, some of these advertisers have already placed their ads using the average rate increase of 22 percent, thereby increasing revenues to 85 percent of normal business," Arturo Librea, the company vice president for finance, said in a letter to the Philippine Stock Exchange.
Advertisments had gone down by 23 percent of normal busines from March 10 to 12, the company said.

"We consider the gain that we will derive from the 22 percent average rate increase will more than compensate for any reduction in business that we have experienced during the past few days," Librea added.
In the same letter, Librea said the disagreement affected primetime placements in Metro Manila. However, non-primetime and provincial slots were not affected.
Officials of the Philippine Association of National Advertisers (Pana) were not available for comment on Monday.

Last week, Pana said orders issued since March 10 were cancelled until the matter was resolved. The group, which has 302 members, said it would be willing to accept a 15 percent increase in advertising rates rather than 22 percent.
